result.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
result.summary: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. Existing harnesses such as VISTA improve the first two, yet turn each model call into at most one action, so the agent acts only as often as its model thinks. We introduce AutoPILOT, which changes the third: in each model call, the model can send a primitive action, start an open-loop macro, or write a closed-loop controller that keeps playing from the screen without further model calls until it hands control back. To evaluate agents in real-time games, we build AFK-Bench, 120 diverse browser games grouped by how they respond to inaction and playable in real time or with the clock paused. With GPT-6.1 Sol under the same budgets, AutoPILOT reaches 68.6% real-time success against 38.3% for VISTA, and on GameWorld it keeps 80.0% in real time while VISTA drops from 84.1% to 42.9%. Its gains hold across models, and it reaches VISTA's final success rate at a fifth of its API cost. Our results suggest that how a harness turns model outputs into actions over time is a central yet underexplored part of agent design, and we hope AutoPILOT and AFK-Bench will serve as a foundation for agents in a world that does not wait.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AutoPILOT 这一视觉智能体执行框架，让模型在一次调用中选择发出原语动作、开环宏操作，或直接编写可在无模型调用下持续接管的闭环控制器，并构建含 120 款浏览器游戏的实时基准 AFK-Bench 进行评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心在于把模型输出转化为跨时间持续起作用的动作状态并压低调用预算，与 LVR 中「昂贵推理调用与轻量过程分离、停止/接管决策及成本核算」的思路可能相关，可供核查能否迁移到动态计算与 THINK/STOP 的代价评估。
